api:
<Harker data={rocks} silica={|r: &Rock| r.silica}>
    <Oxide name="MgO" value={|r: &Rock| r.magnesia} />
    <Oxide name="CaO" value={|r: &Rock| r.lime} />
</Harker>
PropTypeDefault
datarequired
silicaFn(&T) -> f64: SiO₂ in weight %required
children<Oxide name value>: one small plot eachrequired
columnsusize: plots per row3
color, point_sizefirst series colour, 5.
classTailwind classes ("h-64")

Every plot shares the silica axis, so trends line up down a column.

examples.title: Volcanic suite
examples.description: Six oxides against silica, one small plot each.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn volcanic() {
    let data = use_signal(suite());
    rsx! {
        <Harker data={data} silica={|r: &Rock| r.silica} class="h-[520px]">
            <Oxide name="Al₂O₃" value={|r: &Rock| r.alumina} />
            <Oxide name="FeO" value={|r: &Rock| r.iron} />
            <Oxide name="MgO" value={|r: &Rock| r.magnesia} />
            <Oxide name="CaO" value={|r: &Rock| r.lime} />
            <Oxide name="Na₂O" value={|r: &Rock| r.soda} />
            <Oxide name="K₂O" value={|r: &Rock| r.potash} />
        </Harker>
    }
}

examples.title: Basalts
examples.code:
#[component]
fn basalts() {
    let data = use_signal(
        suite()
            .into_iter()
            .filter(|r| r.silica < 55.)
            .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
    );
    rsx! {
        <Harker data={data} silica={|r: &Rock| r.silica} columns={2} color={rgb(0x1e66f5)} class="h-96">
            <Oxide name="MgO" value={|r: &Rock| r.magnesia} />
            <Oxide name="CaO" value={|r: &Rock| r.lime} />
        </Harker>
    }
}
